analysis:
All three changed files are new test-only Swift files under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests. They change no production code, no endpoints, and no key, attestation or authorization handling, so I found no new attack surface or weakened control.

1. PromptTokenCacheTests.swift is a synthetic-tokenizer test suite. It writes fixtures to FileManager.temporaryDirectory under UUID-named directories and removes them afterward. It contains no secrets. It covers a prompt token cache (scope-partitioned, LRU-bounded, env kill-switch, background verification that disables reuse on mismatch). The tests exercise scope partitioning (lines 57-72), which is relevant to T-041 cross-tenant concerns. Those tests only assert behavior (scopes do not share entries) and do not weaken anything. The cache implementation itself (PromptTokenCache, PromptPieceTokenStore, PromptPieceSplitter, PromptTokenCachePolicy) is not in the supplied units. Open questions for integration are whether the production token cache is in-memory only, whether it keys on SHA-256 digests with per-scope partitioning, and whether it shows a hit/miss timing difference across tenants. If it does, that would be a new in-process oracle adjacent to T-041/SEC-035 and should be recorded in the threat model. The tests also cover env passthrough via LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvironment (line 90).

2. InboundChatRequestDecodeTests.swift tests that the merged decode of an inbound chat request equals the separate decode calls, including malformed and rejected bodies. The merged decode's production code is not supplied, so any admission-path behavior divergence is unverified.

3. ServeLoopColdLoadTests.swift (unit 11467a61e66a92b5:0) has only metadata and no text in the supplied evidence. I could not inspect its content. The patch excerpt hints at cold-load admission releasing the coordinator work FIFO, with cancel handling and a single terminal per request, which is availability and ordering behavior relevant to T-010, but nothing is verifiable here.

The production changes (the token cache, merged decode and admission release) were not supplied, so the next pass should review them for cross-tenant timing and cancellation ordering.
